parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Complete the electronic configuration of an isolated gaseous $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name **two** transition elements whose isolated gaseous **atoms** have the same number of electrons in the 3d subshell as an isolated gaseous $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ion.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Cobalt(II) sulfate is added to water to form a pink solution containing complex ion **P**. An excess of concentrated hydrochloric acid is added to this solution to form a blue solution containing complex ion **Q**.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Complete the diagram to show the three-dimensional structure of **Q**. State the charge on this complex ion.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Name the type of reaction in which **P** forms **Q**.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why solutions that contain transition element ions are often coloured.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why the colours of **P** and **Q** are different.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem:
A solution of the bidentate ligand 1,2-diaminoethane, $\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, is added to an aqueous solution of cobalt(II) sulfate. Oxygen is then bubbled into the mixture forming a complex ion with the formula $[\text{Co}(\text{H}_2\text{NCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2)_3]^{3+}$.

This complex ion exists as a mixture of two isomers. The geometry of both of these isomeric complexes is octahedral.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
In this reaction, cobalt undergoes **two** types of reaction. One type of reaction is the same as that described in **(c)(ii)**.

Name the **other** type of reaction that cobalt undergoes.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
(d)(iii)
parts.text: Name the type of stereoisomerism shown by these two isomeric complexes.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text: State the co-ordination number of cobalt in these two isomeric complexes.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
The stability constants, $K_{\text{stab}}$, of three complexes of mercury(II) are given in the table.

| complex | $K_{\text{stab}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Hg}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$ | $2.5 \times 10^{41}$ |
| $[\text{HgCl}_4]^{2-}$ | $1.7 \times 10^{16}$ |
| $[\text{HgI}_4]^{2-}$ | $2.0 \times 10^{30}$ |

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text: Write an expression for the $K_{\text{stab}}$ of $[\text{Hg}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
An aqueous solution containing $\text{Hg}^{2+}$ is added to a solution containing equal concentrations of $\text{CN}^-(\text{aq})$, $\text{Cl}^-(\text{aq})$ and $\text{I}^-(\text{aq})$. The mixture is left to reach equilibrium.

Predict which of the complexes $[\text{Hg}(\text{CN})_4]^{2-}$, $[\text{HgCl}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{HgI}_4]^{2-}$ is present in the resulting mixture in the highest concentration and which is present in the lowest concentration. Explain your answer.
